# Security review: PR #253

Head: ac8a00daf5c0ca017d4fc858e4a0eee5ae72e913
Result: pass-with-notes

No introduced exploitable vulnerability was established under C33's user-account trust boundary. This verdict does not certify per-seat isolation or end-to-end notification delivery.

## Nonblocking findings

1. LOW, confidence 9/10: the suggested close commands interpolate seat and pane directly, rather than calling shell_word. See crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1923 and crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:320. Newly supplied spawn seat IDs are grammar-checked (http/mod.rs:1419), and ordinary launched pane IDs come from tmux's pane-id format, so no external injection path was demonstrated. Existing-ID revive remains a separate input path. C34 follow-up: quote both complete arguments with the existing helper and pin nontrivial inputs. Current tests assert ordinary IDs only (http/tests.rs:3897).

2. LOW, confidence 8/10: unreported notification consumption is keyed only by spawn_id, then the recipient is taken from the registering descriptor's committed parent. See crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:309,324,1513,1833. A different accepted registration sharing that spawn_id can consume the pending notice; the existing different-pane/shared-spawn-id test (http/tests.rs:4375) does not activate inherited waits. No normal-use accidental collision or external exploit was demonstrated, so this is not a same-user impersonation blocker under C33. C34 follow-up: correlate the original launch seat/pane/parent tuple to preserve the stated attribution guarantee.

## Covered contracts and limits

- The new failure details are the eight documented launch/repair fields (http/mod.rs:2076; shape test http/tests.rs:3524). The detached notice/event does not copy environment, argv or captured startup output (registration.rs:328).
- Raw startup output in spawn.failed.last_output and the HTTP diagnostic is retained behavior: merge base 408418a18c1d47b09f77c56059a2f30a1bed64ee already had both sinks (http/mod.rs:1969,1979 at base; :2058,2071 at head). Three additional watch-error branches reach the existing reporter. This review therefore does not promise that arbitrary startup diagnostics are secret-free; the initial introduced-disclosure alert was withdrawn.
- Notification is spawned with cloned services and descriptor, not caller lock guards; the waiter mutex is released when take_unreported returns (registration.rs:309-312; spawn_waits.rs:78).
- Missing, unreadable or tombstoned parent is recorded as withheld: "no live parent"; there is no prime fallback (registration.rs:324-357). Here live means a non-tombstoned registry entry, not freshly proved process liveness.
- Mutex removal gives at-most-once consumption within this daemon, and sequential re-registration deduplication is tested (http/tests.rs:3764). It is not a crash-safe exactly-once delivery transaction.
- Boot inheritance and restart-before-bind reporting are tested (spawn_waits.rs:145; http/tests.rs:3825). The documented --no-wait restart notice is acknowledged noise, not evidence that the spawn failed (docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:187).
- Correctness handoff, not a security finding: registration can observe Waiting, then a timeout using an earlier unbound descriptor can mark Unreported after the only registration hook already ran. See http/mod.rs:1749,1866,1893 and spawn_waits.rs:85,113. The correctness reviewer is being asked to assess this interleaving; it has not been exercised locally.
- No new periodic poll or process launch is claimed. Boot adds one registry scan; registrations add a map check, with detached reporting only for consumed unreported entries. Live resource-cost approval belongs to the performance review.

## Verification

- just pr-freeze 253: PASS, exact requested head, clean detached worktree, remote/GitHub agreement, main base, all five latest checks green.
- GitHub Actions run 44451614497: SUCCESS at this exact head. rust-lint passed fmt and clippy; both Node 22/24 check jobs passed typecheck, lint, tests and native contracts. rust-test reported 2534 passed and 6 skipped.
- Successful rust-test job 135316685425's upload log identifies JUnit artifact 14496016419. Downloaded that exact artifact ID and parsed its XML: the timeout/late-bind, adapter-error, restart-bind, child-exit diagnostics, unchanged success, model-mismatch, boot-filtering and SpawnWaits answer/drop regressions all passed.
- No local build, test, mutation run, harness boot or harness checks was executed, as explicitly required by the review packet. CI proof is not represented as a local harness run. Post-merge live restart proof remains the PR's documented operational step.

## Harness feedback

Read-only review still requires hand-assembling exact-head CI evidence and the successful job's JUnit artifact ID. Observation INS-001 captures a candidate read-only CI-evidence mode that preserves the distinction from local harness checks. No product files were changed for this review.
